title: Fallback weight normalization misalignment causes routes to incompatible model variants
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported requests being routed to model variants that were incompatible with the requested runtime (quantized vs float kernels) during a regional capacity shortage window. Symptoms included elevated 500s for specific tenants, silent quality degradations (mismatched output length/format), and sudden latency spikes when fallback selected a variant that lacked the appropriate execution kernels. Impact spanned Hosted API traffic with cross-tenant fallback into Dedicated and a single Private deployment that had an older variant catalog.

This ticket captures the investigation, short-term mitigations applied, and the permanent fix and rollout plan to prevent recurrence.

2026-02-28 02:23 UTC - Pager duty triggered; on-call routing eng (Liam C.) triaged initial logs.
2026-02-28 02:35 UTC - Observed increased fallback decisions to 'vicuna-13b-quant' for requests originally pinned to 'vicuna-13b-fp16' during eu-west-1 capacity shortage.
2026-02-28 03:05 UTC - Customer-reported garbled outputs; rollback attempted for a targeted tenant mapping rule.
2026-02-28 04:10 UTC - Temporary mitigation: tightened fallback policy to prefer same-precision variants and disabled geo-weight shim.
2026-02-28 06:00 UTC - 500s reduced to baseline; incident declared mitigated.

2026-03-08 - PR for normalization fix and unit tests opened (GH: #14852).
2026-03-12 - Change reviewed; integration tests green; preparing staged rollout to canary hosts.
root_cause: The routing fallback weight normalization function performed integer truncation when computing normalized weights for multi-key fallbacks under high-cardinality policy maps. This truncation introduced a bias such that very small non-zero fallback weights were dropped, causing the comparator to prefer a fallback path with higher nominal priority but incompatible model precision. Two contributing factors: (1) a legacy geo-weight shim that applied additive offsets before normalization (not idempotent) and (2) policy snapshot TTL mismatch between hosted and private catalog sync, which allowed an incompatible variant to be considered a valid target for ~90s after it had been deprecated in the private catalog. The combination made the system select a lower-tier region variant without the required quantized kernel instead of the preferred compatible fallback.
reproduction_steps:
1) Create a policy with three fallback targets: same-region same-precision (weight 0), cross-region same-precision (weight 10), cross-region quantized-variant (weight 11).
2) Simulate capacity shortage by marking primary pool saturated.
3) Apply geo-weight shim that adds +1 to region affinity for cross-region candidate.
4) Run the normalization function on the weight vector in a loop to observe truncation drift under integer cast.
Expected: comparator picks cross-region same-precision.
Observed: comparator picks quantized-variant due to truncation bias and additive shim.
Notes: repro reliably occurs when policy map cardinality > 128 and policy snapshot TTL < 120s.
mitigations_applied:
- Immediate: disabled geo-weight shim globally at 2026-02-28 04:10 UTC.
- Scoped rollback of recently deployed policy merge that changed weight types from floats to fixed-point ints.
- Added a temporary validation to reject fallback candidates whose model precision doesn't match the request's required kernel capability.
- Notified Dedicated and Private owners to refresh model catalogs (hot sync) to avoid TTL window inconsistencies.
permanent_fix_summary:
1) Replace integer-fixed normalization with stable double-precision normalization and deterministic tie-breaker that respects variant capability compatibility.
2) Remove additive (non-idempotent) geo-weight shim; replace with multiplicative scaling applied before normalization.
3) Enforce capability metadata gating in policy evaluator so incompatible variants are filtered before weight normalization.
4) Add cross-environment policy snapshot handshake to guarantee TTLs do not allow deprecated variants to be considered valid for more than 15s.
5) Add end-to-end integration tests covering high-cardinality policy maps and mixed-precision variant pools.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for normalization algorithm with corner cases (zero-sum, tiny weights, high-cardinality).
- Property-based tests to assert normalized weights sum to 1 within epsilon and preserve rank order when capability differences exist.
- Integration tests that simulate hosted->dedicated->private fallback across catalog versions.
- Canary rollout in eu-west-1 with canary traffic fraction 1% for 24h, then 10% for 6h, then full rollout.
- Add synthetic tenants in staging to replicate FinQ's traffic pattern and verify no misroutes.
rollout_plan:
- Merge to release branch runtime-1.24 after QA signoff.
- Deploy to canary cluster in eu-west-1 (hosts: canary-rt-1/2).
- Monitor routing decision histogram, fallback rates, 5xx, and tenant-specific error rates for 48h.
- If stable, increment canary to 10% and monitor for 24h.
- Full rollout across regions after zero regressions for 72h.
- Post-deploy: coordinate private deployment customer upgrade notes and provide an opt-in validator tool for their catalogs.
monitoring:
Add new metrics and alerts:
- routing.normalization.error_rate (should be ~0).
- routing.fallback_to_incompatible_variant_count.
- policy.snapshot_ttl_variance_by_env.
- per-tenant fallback latency and 5xx ratio.
Dashboards: create 'Fallback Safety' dashboard and add tenant filter for top 50 customers.
SLO change: create alert if FallBack->IncompatibleVariant > 0.05% over 5m.
notes:
Customer communication: Sent initial incident summary and temporary mitigation notes to FinQ and 2 other affected customers on 2026-02-28. Scheduled follow-up postmortem with customers on 2026-03-18.
Operational follow-ups: schedule a 90-day audit of all fallback weight changes and enforce code owner review on any changes to normalization logic.
